name: Silberbergwerk Schwaz
kurzbeschreibung: Visitor mine in Schwaz: 90-minute guided tour with the mine railway 800 m deep into the Falkenstein – once Europe's most significant silver and copper mining area.
beschreibung:
The Schwaz Silver Mine in Schwaz is considered one of Europe's most important historic mines. In the 15th and 16th centuries, Schwaz was Europe's mining center: around 1500, the city had over 20,000 inhabitants and was the second-largest settlement in the Habsburg Empire after Vienna. The 15,7 tonnes of fine silver extracted in 1523 accounted for around 85 percent of global production at the time. The Fugger family from Augsburg played a decisive role in mining at the Falkenstein.

During the approximately 90-minute tour, visitors ride the mine railway about 800 meters into the mountain, where a constant 12°C prevails year-round. They then walk roughly 1,000 meters through the tunnel; helmets and coats are provided. The tour offers insight into the lives of miners during the silver boom. For groups of 20 or more, advance reservation is recommended. Adults pay €23 including the tour, children aged 5 to 14 pay €15.
